newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine mills well-stocked wait for wheat fall.
newsitem.headline: Philippine mills well-stocked wait for wheat fall.

text.p: Philippine flour millers are expected to adopt a wait-and-see attitude to the wheat market next week despite the recent softening of U.S. wheat prices, traders said on Friday.
"Wheat prices slipped slightly this week and millers are waiting for prices to dip further," said one trader.
Some flour millers asked for daily price quotations during the week but there were no transactions.
"Buyers were just having a peek but there were no actual tenders made," said one trader.
Traders said most local millers remain fully stocked affording them the luxury of waiting.

The Department of Trade and Industry said the prevailing retail price of hard flour in Metro Manila is 290 pesos ($11.15) per 25 kg. The retail price of soft flour softened to 260 pesos ($10) from 285 pesos ($10.96) last week.

The state-run National Food Authority said that the average retail price of white corn rose to 10.75 pesos (41.35 cents) per kg from 10.67 pesos (41.03 cents), while yellow corn remained at 10.84 pesos (41.7 cents) a kg.
